handedness.visual_basis: Lead side appears on viewer left (golfer's left) throughout — typical right-handed stance with left side closer to target.

evidence.visual_basis: Hands during the downswing are clearly farther from the body than at address — hands move outward toward the ball.
Hands continue on an outward path away from the torso, increasing gap between hands and chest.
Shaft on the downswing appears noticeably steeper than the forearm — club sits above the arm in delivery frames.
Club shaft is upright compared to the forearm as it approaches the ball, indicating a steep delivery.
Some opening of the angle between lead forearm and shaft visible before the hands reach the ball — partial early release beginning.
Wrist hinge appears reduced as the clubhead moves forward through impact area, suggesting early release.
